name: Cuban-Style Black Beans and Rice
pitch: This classic combo is simple, hearty, and totally satisfying — garlic and cumin do the heavy lifting here.
steps: Cook your rice according to package directions.
While the rice cooks, heat a splash of oil in a saucepan over medium heat and sauté 3–4 minced garlic cloves for about a minute until fragrant.
Add the black beans (with their liquid if canned, or with a splash of water if cooked from scratch), plus a generous pinch of cumin, salt, and pepper.
Simmer the beans for 10–15 minutes until slightly thickened and saucy.
Spoon the beans over the rice and serve — a splash of vinegar stirred into the beans at the end really brightens the whole dish!

name: Black Bean Rice Patties
pitch: Crispy on the outside, soft on the inside — these little pan-fried patties are a fun, hands-on dinner that kids tend to love.
steps: Cook your rice if it isn't already, then let it cool slightly — leftover rice works even better here.
Mash the black beans in a bowl until mostly smooth but still a little chunky.
Mix in the cooked rice, a few pinches of garlic powder, cumin, salt, and pepper until it holds together. If it feels too loose, add a little more rice.
Form the mixture into palm-sized patties.
Heat oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and fry the patties 3–4 minutes per side until golden and crispy.
Serve as-is or with a drizzle of soy sauce mixed with a little vinegar as a quick dipping sauce.

name: Black Bean Rice Soup
pitch: A warm, filling soup that comes together fast — it's humble but genuinely comforting on a busy weeknight.
steps: Heat oil in a medium pot over medium heat and cook 3–4 cloves of minced garlic for 1 minute.
Add the black beans and about 3 cups of water (or more for a thinner soup), then season with cumin, a pinch of smoked paprika if you have it, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a simmer and let it cook for 10 minutes, then use a spoon or ladle to mash some of the beans against the side of the pot to naturally thicken the broth.
Stir in the cooked rice and simmer another 5 minutes until everything is warmed through and the soup has a nice, thick consistency.
Taste, adjust salt, and finish with a small splash of vinegar to brighten it up before serving.
